questions: Is the cost 'i' the position index (1-based) of the left element being swapped, or is it the value of the element at position i (P_i)?

When swapping P_i and P_{i+1}, does the cost i refer to the index before the swap (which remains constant) or does it refer to the index of the element that ends up at position i after the swap (which could change if many swaps occur)?
Does 'ascending order' mean strictly increasing (1,2,...,N) or non-decreasing (allowing duplicates, though duplicates are not possible given it's a permutation)?
Is the goal to achieve the sorted permutation with the minimum total cost, or is any sequence of swaps that results in sorted order acceptable (with its total cost)?
If multiple minimal-cost sequences exist, can we output any of their total costs (they are equal), or is there a unique minimal total cost?
Are we allowed to perform swaps that increase the cost unnecessarily as long as we eventually sort it, or must we strictly minimize the total cost?
Does the cost accumulate as the sum of i for each swap, where i is the position index at the time of that swap, even if earlier swaps changed which elements are at those indices?
Is the operation allowed only on adjacent positions, and does the cost depend on the distance between the swapped elements (always 1) or something else?
